summary: Split-payload dropper: unused mandatory dependency paired with opaque bundled blob
details: iterquarry 2.2.1 declares a mandatory unpinned dependency on the sibling PyPI package `libseal` in its pyproject, and ships a 27 KB opaque high-entropy binary file `src/iterquarry/quarry.libseal` as package-data. No module within iterquarry's own source imports `libseal` or references the `.libseal` file, so the dependency serves no function inside this package. The structural shape is a split-payload dropper: the carrier package stores an encrypted blob while a sibling dependency named for the blob's extension acts as the loader. Any installer of iterquarry resolves and installs whatever `libseal` currently publishes to PyPI, and that package is the natural consumer of the bundled blob next to the Python modules. The payload is unreadable from this package alone — the loader lives outside its reviewable source, defeating per-package static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
